study_identification_part.si_4_title: Normative Modeling of Brain Morphometry in Clinical High Risk for Psychosis

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Primary normative models used multivariable fractional polynomial regression (MFPR) in the CentileBrain framework; robustness analyses also repeated normative analyses using gaussian process regression (GPR) and generalized additive models for location, scale, and shape (GAMLSS).
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text:
Through this pipeline, we identified multivariable fractional polynomial regression as the optimal algorithm; the optimal covariate combination involved site harmonization (ComBat-GAM [combatting batch effects-generalized additive model]) 23 and the inclusion of intracranial volume, mean CT, and mean SA in the models of the regional measures of SV, CT, and SA, respectively.
We tested the robustness of the results to the spatial resolution of the input data and algorithm by repeating the normative analyses using the Schaeffer400-parcels atlas or gray and white matter maps as input features and gaussian process regression or generalized additive models for location, scale, and shape as alternate algorithms (eMethods in Supplement 1).
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Haas2024.pdf.md: Methods / Normative modeling framework; Haas2024.pdf.md: Methods / Additional analyses

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: FreeSurfer-derived regional cortical thickness, cortical surface area, and subcortical volume measures.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Images were parcellated and segmented at each respective site using standard pipelines implemented using FreeSurfer analysis software (https://surfer.nmr.mgh.harvard.edu/) to yield regional measures of cortical thickness (CT), cortical surface area (SA), and subcortical volume (SV) (eTable 6).

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age was the initial explanatory variable; site harmonization was applied via ComBat-GAM; model optimization added ICV (SV models), mean cortical thickness (CT models), and mean cortical surface area (SA models).
